200.description:
An agency's public home page (`/gems/{slug},{st}/buyer/public/home`, or `/gems/buyer/public/home?syndicatedOrgId=..&region=..` for syndicated agencies): name, region, the agency's own website and logo when published, the portal URLs, and the fact that the page's open-bid table itself is behind a supplier login (`open_bids_login_required` is always true; use `list_agency_open_bids` for the anonymous widget). An unknown agency id is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agency_id` | string |  |
| `home_url` | string |  |
| `kind` | string |  |
| `logo_url` | string | Portal logo URL (`/gems/docviewer/logo/{orgId}/{fileId}`, redirects to fs.thepublicgroup.com); null when the page shows no logo. |
| `name` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `open_bids_login_required` | boolean | The page's own open-bid table asks for a supplier login on every agency observed. |
| `public_bids_url` | string | The anonymous open-bid widget URL for native agencies; null for syndicated agencies, which have none. |
| `region` | string |  |
| `region_name` | string |  |
| `source_url` | string |  |
| `syndicated_org_id` | number | Numeric org id for syndicated agencies; null for native ones. |
| `website_url` | string | The agency's own website linked from its logo; null when the page links nowhere (observed as `http://` for syndicated agencies). |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
List every agency Public Purchase files under one region: native agencies hosted on the portal (slug ids such as `bellevue,wa`, with a public open-bid widget) and syndicated agencies hosted elsewhere (ids such as `syndicated:6252,ut`, home page only). One fragment per region, no pagination; California is the largest with about 1,100 rows. A region code the site does not know is `not_found`; a known region with no agencies is a valid empty list.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `agencies` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agency_id` | string | Id for `get_agency` / `list_agency_open_bids`: the site's path segment for native agencies (`bellevue,wa`), `syndicated:{orgId},{st}` for syndicated ones. |
| `home_url` | string | The agency's public home page on the portal. |
| `kind` | string | native: hosted on Public Purchase with a public open-bid widget; syndicated: an agency hosted on another system, home page only. |
| `name` | string | Agency name exactly as the directory prints it (the site does not normalise these; a few are junk entered by the agency). |
| `public_bids_url` | string | The anonymous open-bid widget URL (native agencies only); null for syndicated agencies. |
| `syndicated_org_id` | number | The site's numeric org id for syndicated agencies; null for native ones. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

agency_id.description: Native agency id as the site's path segment, e.g. `bellevue,wa` or `uintahco,ut` (from `list_agencies`). `syndicated:...` ids are accepted by the schema but rejected as invalid input: those agencies have no widget. Pattern: ^([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*|syndicated:[0-9]+),[A-Za-z]{2}$.

url.description: Alternatively, a pasted agency page URL such as https://www.publicpurchase.com/gems/bellevue,wa/buyer/public/home; the agency id is read from the path.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
Open bids a native agency publishes through its anonymous public widget (`/gems/{agency_id}/buyer/public/publicInfo`): bid id, title, short description, start and end dates (agency-local, with the zone abbreviation the site prints and an ISO 8601 form with offset), time left, addendum dates and the detail URL (which requires a supplier login). The widget returns every public open bid at once; there is no pagination, sorting or closed-bid history. Only agencies that enabled the widget expose rows (roughly 1 in 20 in the Utah/Washington census); the others answer a valid empty list. Syndicated agencies (`syndicated:...` ids) have no widget and are rejected as invalid input. An unknown agency id is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `bids` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addenda` | object[] | Addendum issue dates in the order printed; empty when the site prints `No Addendums`. |
| `bid_id` | string | The site's global numeric bid id (from the detail link's `bidId`). |
| `description` | string | Short description shown in the title's tooltip, HTML entities decoded; null when the widget carries none. |
| `detail_login_required` | boolean | The detail page answers 401 and redirects to the supplier login without an account. |
| `detail_url` | string | Bid detail page on the portal (`/gems/{agency}/bid/bidView?bidId=..`). |
| `end_date` | string | ISO 8601 form of `end_date_text` with offset; null when the zone abbreviation is not mapped. |
| `end_date_text` | string | Closing date exactly as printed, agency-local. |
| `start_date` | string | ISO 8601 form of `start_date_text` with the UTC offset implied by its North American zone abbreviation; null when the abbreviation is not one the program maps. |
| `start_date_text` | string | Start date exactly as printed, agency-local, e.g. `Sep 17, 2026 9:00:00 AM PDT`. |
| `time_left_text` | string | Remaining time as printed when the page was served, e.g. `3 days 1 hour`. |
| `time_zone_abbr` | string | Zone abbreviation the site printed on the end date (`PDT`, `MDT`, ...); null when none. |
| `title` | string | Bid title as listed, e.g. `ITB #26078 - Robinswood Playground`. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

bids.description: The work to be performed by the Consultant consists of preparing preliminary engineering design, and environmental study, permitting and developing 30%, 60%, 90%, and final design plans, specifications, and estimates (PS&E) for improvements on SE Eastgate Way Sidewalk between Richards Road and 13212 SE Eastgate Way. The major features of the project are as follows: • Evaluate alternative cross sections: including lane width, shoulders, bike lane, width of planters, sidewalk width, barrier, and retaining wall type. • Develop criteria and select a preferred alternative. • Develop 30%, 60%, 90%, and final design plans, specifications and cost estimates. • Complete environmental study and permitting • Provide design support during construction • Other improvements and work associated with the sidewalk include, but are not limited to, site preparation, erosion and sediment control, storm drainage system, flow control and water quality facilities, environmentally sensitive area impact mitigation, irrigation, landscaping, channelization, retaining walls, signing, traffic control, and other mitigation as required. The A&E Professional Services Agreement with the successful Consultant firm will conform to all requirements outlined in the Using Consultants chapter of the WSDOT Local Agency Guideline (LAG) Manual. This project is federally funded. This project has zero percent as an FSBE Goal and a voluntary ten percent SBE goal.

bids.description: INTRODUCTION The City of Bellevue (the “City”) is requesting competitive proposals from qualified firms for solid waste collection services within the City Service Area. These services include: residential and commercial garbage, recycling, and organics (yard debris and food scraps) collection, the delivery of garbage to a King County facility per the City’s interlocal agreement, and the processing and marketing of collected recyclables and organics. The initial contract term will be for ten (10) years, from July 1, 2028 to June 30, 2038, with a City option for an extension of up to two (2) years. Terms used in this RFP that are defined in the Contract have the meanings assigned to them therein. Defined terms are applicable to both the singular and plural. EXISTING COLLECTION SYSTEM This section generally describes the existing solid waste collection system operated under the current contract. Carefully review Brief Scope of Services, Attachment “A”, and the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A) to determine the scope of operations envisioned under the new Contract. The City’s current contract with Republic Services is available to Proposers upon request. The City of Bellevue has a residential population of approximately 158,000 with approximately 30,800 single-family residential customers and approximately 2,000 multi-family, commercial, and drop-box accounts. The existing collection system is operated under contract with total contractor billings of approximately $37 million in 2025. Garbage collection is voluntary for generators within the City. Single-family Collection Single-family residences are provided weekly garbage collection under a variable rate structure. Under the new contract, Residents will be required to use a contractor-provided garbage cart for basic service, but may use their own containers for extra material. There are approximately 200 single-family residential customers who currently use their own container who will need to transition to a contractor-provided container. Weekly single-family recycling collection is included as part of garbage collection service. Most recyclable materials are placed in the recycling cart except for small appliances and electronics, textiles, and large metal items. Weekly single-family organics (i.e., yard debris and food scraps) collection is also included as part of basic collection services, through the use of 96-gallon carts. Customers may also use Kraft bags and place bundled or boxed materials at the curb as well as rent additional yard debris carts from the Contractor if more than one cart is needed. Customers may set out up to 192 gallons of material per collection, with additional materials accepted for a charge. Non-garbage customers may also subscribe to either or both recycling and organics collection services on a fee-for-service basis. The City has an assignable right to the carts used under the current contract and will assign the ownership of those carts to the Contractor performing services under the new contract. As described in Section 4.1.3 of the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A), bill assistance is to be provided to eligible single-family residential customers by the Contractor billing these Customers a reduced percentage of the regular rate for the subscribed service level. The estimated approximate number of eligible Single-family Residential customers and respective rate reductions are: 70% Rate Reduction: 450 Single-family Residential customers (Senior (62+) households at 50% or less of area median income). 35% Rate Reduction: 1,250 Single-family Residential customers (80% or less of area median income). Commercial and Multi-family Collection Multi-family complexes are provided with commercial garbage services, as well as a recycling and organics program that accepts most of the same materials handled by the single-family recycling program. Commercial and Multi-family Complex garbage collection is provided through the use of customer-owned containers and drop-box compactors, as well as contractor-owned carts, detachable containers, and drop-boxes. A range of sizes and collection frequencies are available. Commercial and Multi-family Complex customers currently are provided unlimited recycling and one hundred ninety-two gallons (192) of organics collection per week, via cart service, per garbage container. The City anticipates offering a bill assistance program for multi-family residents. The planned program has a rebate structure and will be funded and directly implemented by the City. There are no rate reductions for the Contractor to implement in regard to this multi-family resident bill assistance program. Disposal All collected garbage is currently delivered to the King County Disposal System per the City/County Interlocal Agreement. Administration The City is responsible for overall solid waste program administration, including managing the collection contract and providing solid waste education and promotion to the public. These activities are funded through an administrative fee and targeted program fees paid to the City, as provided for in the current contract. This system of funding will change under the new contract to a single annual contract fee paid by the contractor to the City. These programs have traditionally been performed through in-house staff or the use of consultants. The solid waste collection contractor is responsible for providing all services, including, but not limited to, customer service, customer billing, distributing public notices about collection service and schedule changes, such as holiday hours, billing adjustment notices, and other service-related communications, as described in the draft 2028 Contract (Exhibit A). RFP Exhibits: Exhibit A provides the draft 2028 Contract, which details all the services expected to be performed by the future contractor. Exhibit B provides 2025 collection data by sector/collection program and customer container counts. Exhibit C provides 2026 rates charged by the current contractor to all sectors of customers. Proposal Form 2A provides a listing of service levels desired under the new Contract and customer counts (where available) for services provided under the current contract. The customer counts provided on Form 2A have been reported by the current contractor, and unless noted otherwise in the instructions or footnotes to Proposal Form 2A, are accurate to the best of the City’s knowledge. RFP OBJECTIVES The City has identified the following objectives for future solid waste services: Alignment with best practices Responsive to community needs: reliability, affordability, user experience Compliance with state laws and local policy Leverage technology and data Along with these objectives, the City also intends to maintain key contract elements, including weekly collection services for single-family residents and an embedded rate structure. The RFP structure and terms, sample base contract, proposed alternatives, and evaluation process are intended to support these objectives.
bids.title: RFP #26039 - Solid Waste Services

bids.description: The City is seeking a highly qualified Design-Build Team with progressive design build experience and strong skills in creativity and collaboration that will engage as critical, integrated team members throughout design and construction of a large-scale landscape project (Phase 1) and leading design of the aquatic center (Phase 2). The Bellevue Airfield Park Project (the 'Project') site is located largely within the I-90 commercial district, near the Lake to Lake Trail and major transportation corridors. The Master Plan for this community park includes trails, wooded picnic areas, a playground, splash pad, flexible lawn play, basketball and pickleball courts, and a new regional aquatic center able to support the demand for recreational and competitive swimming in Bellevue and the broader region. The Apprentice Utilization Requirement for the Project will be 15%.
bids.title: RFQ #26020 - Bellevue Airfield Park Project

bids.description: This project includes renovation of Streetscape landscaping along 148th Ave NE, between NE 8th St and NE 12th St. The scope of work includes clear and grubbing, TESC measures, irrigation elements, soil amendments, planting, and mulching. It is the responsibility of the contractor to provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, disposal, service operations, and expertise required to complete this project for the City of Bellevue in accordance with specifications and site plans. Follow project milestones for ROW landscape inspections checklist, provided at construction pre-con. SEE BID DOCS FOR DETAILED INFOMATION
bids.title: ITQ #26098 - 148th Ave NE, Landscape Renovation

bids.description: This project involves pruning and crown cleaning for up to 168 street trees and removing up to 11 within the northern Bellevue CBD Right-of-Way. Nine trees require only limited dead-wood pruning. Work is time-and-materials with a not-to-exceed limit, and all pruning must follow ISA ANSI A300 and ANSI Z133.1 standards under the supervision of an ISA Certified Arborist, with at least one arborist on-site at all times. Traffic control is required. The City will provide the ROW permit and draft traffic control plans, but the contractor is responsible for all traffic control needed to meet final permit requirements, including any adjustments by the ROW Inspector or needs for Uniformed Police Officers. Contractors must provide all labor, materials, equipment, and disposal necessary to complete the project per City specifications. SEE BID DOCS FOR MORE DETAILS
bids.title: ITQ #26105 - 2026 North CBD Cycle Pruning

bids.description: Work contemplated to be performed under this contract is as follows: Interior renovation of the Crossroads Community Center kitchen and teen room. Kitchen work includes new equipment and hood and associated structural modifications, roof penetration and installation of hood exhaust, and new cabinets as well as limited electrical, plumbing and mechanical scope. Electrical and plumbing scope require separate trade permit by Contractor. Teen room includes partition demolition, interior door and window reconfiguration and new finishes. Engineer's Estimate Range is $400,000 - $500,000. Attendance at a Pre-Bid site walk/inspection and sign-in by Prime/General Contractors who intend to submit a bid for Work on this project will be held at: 2:00 P.M., October 8th 2026 Crossroads Community Center-16000 NE 10th Bellevue WA 98008
bids.title: Bid #26092 - Crossroads Community Center Teaching Kitchen and Teen Room Renovation
